opportunities.title: New-project intake and triage agent across engineering, MRD lab and tech lines
opportunities.problem: Every new assignment enters through one of three unstructured, human-read channels - a generic Wix 'submit an assignment' form, a callback request, or the project-team line at 732-429-1293 - with no qualification questionnaire, no scheduling, no acknowledgment automation and no visible case record. A person must read each inquiry, work out which division and which of ~32 Professional Engineers it belongs to (automotive failure, fire/explosion origin, structural, electrical, metallurgy, friction, accident reconstruction), and reply. The site itself routes urgency to the phone ('call now ... for Immediate Assistance'), which means fire and explosion losses that arrive after hours queue until someone reads a form.
evidence: Three parallel intake paths with no scheduling, quote calculator or client portal - 'the only web intake mechanisms are Wix forms plus mailto links' and the form only promises the office 'will contact you directly' (https://www.aelgroup.net/newprojects)
Team page and projects page push phone contact for urgent work rather than an online booking path (https://www.aelgroup.net/team-members)
Engineering division spans at least nine distinct technical service lines, so routing an inquiry to the right PE is a classification decision, not a hand-off (https://www.aelgroup.net/engineering)

Three divisions run under separate brands, emails and phone numbers (aelgroup.net, affiliatedinc.net lab inbox, affiliatedtech.com), so one client relationship splits across inboxes and lines (https://www.aelgroup.net/contact-mrd)
No office hours, after-hours coverage or response-time commitment is published, consistent with intake not being an owned, measured process (https://www.aelgroup.net/)
The sister technology division already resells AI call summarisation and transcription, so call-derived text is an available input rather than new infrastructure (https://www.affiliatedtech.com/ai)
opportunities.agent_design: Trigger: a new form submission, an email to the new-project or lab inbox, or a transcribed voicemail from the project line. The agent extracts matter type, loss/incident date, jurisdiction, referring party (law firm, insurer, industrial client), evidence available, deadline and conflict-relevant parties; classifies against the nine service lines; proposes the best-fit case team from a structured PE capability matrix; drafts a fee/engagement outline from prior similar matters; sends an acknowledgment with next steps and a booking link; opens a case record and notifies the duty manager. Human approval: the duty manager approves or amends the case team and any fee commitment before the client sees it; the agent never quotes a firm price or accepts an engagement. Time-critical fire/explosion/vehicle matters trigger an SMS/page escalation to an on-call engineer instead of sitting in an inbox.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: This is not a chat widget - it needs a persistent case record, write access to three separate mail domains plus telephony/voicemail transcripts, calendar booking, an expertise/availability model over 32 engineers, and conflict screening before the agent says anything to a prospective client. A subscription chatbot has no record of state, cannot route across divisions, and will confidently mis-assign a metallurgy matter to a structural engineer.

impact_estimate.range: $19,000-$31,000 per year of administrative labour, plus unmodelled revenue-at-risk reduction on time-sensitive losses
impact_estimate.assumptions: Inference: intake/coordination consumes roughly 0.3-0.5 of one full-time non-technical coordinator's time at a 32-PE, three-division firm with no CRM. Valued at NJ median $47,740 for Customer Service Representatives (the closest published proxy for client-intake desk work), loaded 1.3x for benefits = ~$62,000, i.e. $19k-$31k. Excludes any gain from faster quote turnaround or avoided missed assignments, which we cannot size without case volume. No revenue or case-count data is public, so this is a wage-based band only.

opportunities.pilot_scope: 2-4 weeks: agent live on one channel only (the new-project web form plus the newproject@ inbox), classifying matter type and proposing division + PE + urgency tier, drafting the acknowledgment email for staff approval, and writing every inquiry into a single case log with a response-time stamp. Deliverable includes a PE capability matrix built from the 32 published bios and a weekly report of response times and mis-routes, which becomes the baseline for phase two.

opportunities.title: PE report-drafting desk: retrieval over the firm's own reports, lab data and standards
opportunities.problem: AEL's output is a bespoke long-form technical report per matter, and the firm is explicitly hiring for the capacity to produce it. Throughput therefore scales with licensed authoring hours, not with inbound demand - and there is no visible internal knowledge layer: no case-study library, no blog, and the public site is a 75-URL Wix build maintained ad hoc (one bio page still carries 'Title Here' placeholder text). Each new failure analysis has to re-derive background, test rationale and discussion text that an earlier matter already covered.
evidence: Careers page is recruiting licensed PEs with 5+ years' experience to investigate, review evidence and write, with explicit emphasis on verbal, analytical and writing skills - hiring for report-producing capacity (https://www.aelgroup.net/careers)

Engineering service lines (automotive failure analysis, fire/explosion origin and causation, structural, electrical, metallurgical, friction, accident reconstruction) all terminate in written cause-and-origin findings (https://www.aelgroup.net/engineering)

The in-house lab generates the underlying evidence - SEM with EDS, light optical microscopy, metallography, mechanical/hardness, corrosion, XRD/XRF/FTIR, soil - so test results feed straight into report narrative (https://www.aelgroup.net/lab-services)

No document library, case-study archive or knowledge base is exposed; the sitemap is dominated by one-off pages and per-initial bios, indicating no content/knowledge system (https://www.aelgroup.net/pages-sitemap.xml)

Industry survey: 68% of engineering firm leaders estimate AI could automate up to 29% of current tasks, with marketing/sales and proposal-type drafting the leading use case and design/project delivery at only 36% (https://www.acec.org/resource/new-acec-research-institute-report-finds-ai-is-transforming-engineering-by-accelerating-human-talent/)
opportunities.agent_design: A private, permission-scoped retrieval layer over the firm's own past reports, lab worksheets, photo sets, standards and expert CVs. Triggers: a new case file or a lab result set is attached to a matter. The agent produces a structured first draft - scope and background, evidence examined, test methods and results summary, discussion of candidate failure mechanisms with citations to the firm's own prior analyses and to standards - in house style, with every paragraph carrying a provenance link to the source document and page. It assembles the credentials appendix and the exhibit/test-record list, and flags statements with no supporting source instead of writing around them. Human approval: the responsible Professional Engineer reviews, edits and seals every report; the agent cannot issue, sign or certify anything, and drafts are watermarked as unreviewed.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: Three hard blockers. (1) Confidentiality: litigation files, insurer materials and NDAs mean the corpus cannot leave the firm's control, which argues for private/on-prem inference. (2) Provenance: an expert report may be tested in deposition or discovery, so each sentence needs a traceable source - a generic assistant cannot show it and will invent a citation. (3) The jagged-frontier evidence: in a field experiment with 758 consultants, AI users were significantly more likely to get the answer wrong on the one task deliberately placed outside the model's capability, which is exactly the failure mode that would destroy an expert's credibility. Guardrails, retrieval scoping and PE sign-off are engineering work, not a subscription.

impact_estimate.range: $28,000-$56,000 per year of licensed engineer authoring time (conservative); upper bound ~$70,000 if the higher 20% end of the range holds across six authors
impact_estimate.assumptions: Inference: 3-6 of the 32 listed PEs spend roughly 1,400 hours a year each on report authoring, and retrieval-assisted drafting removes 10-20% of those hours. At NJ median $104,660 ($50.32/hr) for civil engineers, 4 PEs x 1,400 hrs = 5,600 hrs; 10-20% = 560-1,120 hrs = $28k-$56k. We deliberately stay well below the 29% task-automation ceiling that engineering firm leaders self-report and far below the 40% time reduction seen on 20-30 minute professional writing tasks in a controlled experiment (Science 2023, https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.adh2586, paywalled) because those tasks are not sealed forensic reports. Excludes any throughput/revenue upside from accepting more matters, which is the actual strategic value.

opportunities.pilot_scope: 3-4 weeks: ingest 20-40 de-identified past reports plus lab worksheets for one service line (metallurgical/materials is the cleanest, since the MRD lab already produces structured results) into a private retrieval index, and ship a drafting assistant for two sections only - 'evidence examined' and 'test results summary' - with per-paragraph source links. Success measure: measured drafting hours per report versus a pre-pilot baseline on 5 live matters, plus PE-reported edit burden. No client-facing output in the pilot.

opportunities.title: Expert-matching and CV/credentials packet agent for case staffing
opportunities.problem: Putting an expert in front of a prospective client is a manual, one-engineer-at-a-time process: each of the 32 bio pages carries a 'Request CV' / 'Request Engineer on New Project' action that routes a request through email or a form to a person, who then finds the CV, checks the engineer's availability, and assembles a package. Nothing publishes availability, licensing by state, testimony history or CV versions in a queryable form, and because the three divisions sit behind different brands, inboxes and phone numbers, assembling a multi-disciplinary team (forensic engineer + lab testing + technology forensics) means stitching across them by hand.
evidence: CV and expert-placement requests are handled engineer-by-engineer through a per-bio 'Request CV / Request Engineer on New Project' action routed via email/forms, not a system (https://www.aelgroup.net/bpl)
Team page lists 32 named Professional Engineers and Ph.D. staff plus one non-PE name, each on a separate bio page with no titles or availability published (https://www.aelgroup.net/team-members)
Divisions publish separate emails and numbers, so a multi-division team has no shared record (https://www.aelgroup.net/contact-mrd)
Scope includes expert witness testimony and consulting 'worldwide', which multiplies per-matter credential, travel and licensing coordination (https://www.aelgroup.net/)

Growth signal: a New York professional-service registration at the Edison address (June 2025) implies a second state's licensing and expert-disclosure requirements now apply (https://opengovny.com/corporation/7636063) - flagged as second-hand in the research profile, aggregator page was not reachable at source
opportunities.agent_design: A structured expert registry (licenses and expiry by state, disciplines, testimony and deposition history, publication list, current CV version, availability and travel constraints) becomes the single source of truth, seeded from the 32 public bios and maintained by staff. Triggers: a new case record, or a staff request such as 'who can cover a fire-origin matter in Nassau County next month'. The agent ranks candidates against the matter, runs a name/party conflict check, generates the CV package and fee schedule from templates, drafts the engagement letter, checks the engineer's licence is current in the relevant state, and holds a calendar slot. Human approval: a principal approves the proposed expert and signs the engagement; the agent never commits an engineer's time or represents a credential it cannot source.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: The value is in a versioned, queryable data model plus rules, not in conversation: licence expiry enforcement, conflict screening, CV version control and calendar holds all need write access to real systems and an audit trail. An LLM answering from unstructured PDFs will happily quote a lapsed licence or an out-of-date CV, which in an expert-witness setting is a credibility and liability event. It also has to join three separately branded inboxes, which no off-the-shelf assistant does.

impact_estimate.range: $5,000-$20,000 per year of coordination time, plus unmodelled risk reduction on credential/licence errors
impact_estimate.assumptions: Inference: 8-15 CV/placement requests a month, at 1-3 hours of assembly and availability-chasing each, equals roughly 96-540 hours a year; valued at $50.32/hr (NJ civil engineer median, since the chaser is usually technical staff) = $4.8k-$27k, narrowed to $5k-$20k. If the work is instead done by an HR/recruiting-style coordinator, the NJ median for Human Resources Specialists ($80,690, https://www.onetonline.org/link/localwages/13-1071.00?st=NJ) would put it materially higher, but we did not assume that. Request volume is not public; the band assumes AEL's stated litigation- and insurance-driven demand.

opportunities.pilot_scope: 2-3 weeks: build the expert registry for the top 10 most-requested PEs from their public bios plus staff-supplied licence and availability data, then ship (a) a natural-language match query across the registry and (b) one-click generation of a branded CV + credentials packet with a licence-expiry check. Measured on turnaround time per request versus the current email/form path.

lead_score.rationale: Pain (20/30): the operating evidence is strong and structural - three parallel manual intake channels with no scheduling or portal, per-engineer CV requests by email, a hiring signal that points at authoring capacity, three brands behind separate inboxes. But it is inferred from the firm's own architecture, not stated: no customer reviews, no complaint themes, no case volumes, no revenue, so we cannot show that anyone has named this as a problem. Fit (17/20): opportunities A, C and D map squarely onto what this consultancy builds, and the materials-testing lab plus the in-house telecom arm give an unusually clean data and telephony substrate; only physical/edge AI (E) has no evidence. Ability to pay (13/20): 51-200 employees with 32 licensed PEs, licensed in NJ and registered in NY, and a profitable-looking expert-witness line whose bill rates are far above the wage benchmarks used here - but revenue, backlog and systems spend are all unknown, and a firm that has stayed on Wix may be genuinely cost-averse; the tech division could also in-source. Ease (9/15): single Edison facility and a very low technical baseline make a pilot easy to scope, but no owner, president or GM is published anywhere, so there is no identified buyer, and anything touching reports needs a PE champion. Strategic (12/15): the pattern is highly repeatable - physical-failure forensic engineering and materials-testing practices are a dense, well-defined niche across the NY/NJ metro, and the intake-plus-report-provenance architecture sells again to each one; AEL's tech division is also a potential reseller channel rather than just a client. Discounted for the missing decision-maker and the thin outcome data.

best_evidence_signal: The careers page is recruiting licensed PEs specifically to investigate, review evidence and write - i.e. report-authoring capacity is the growth constraint - while intake still runs through three manual channels with no scheduling or portal (https://www.aelgroup.net/careers)
